Tubing, plugs,and a shaft. Print the roller.

A parametric intake roller. Set the tube, the layout, and the shaft. Download a plate and a flexure plug. The model is built in your browser.

01 / Roller

Geometry

Every tube trails the same way around the hub. 25° is a short trail. 75° is close to tangent with the rim.

Width is the full roller, from outer face to outer face.

02 / Tubing

What you cut

Material is for your cut list. It does not change the printed parts.

03 / Attachment

Plug and shaft

Plug length is the whole printed plug. Part of the base stays in the collar or hub socket. The rest slides into the tube.

Use 0 for a solid plug, or 2 to 8 slots. One slot does not leave fingers that can spread.

Start and end are measured from the plug base. The slots begin at the tube end. They can stop before the tip.

The plug is the shaft that enters the tube. Each ridge ramps up toward the tip so the tube can slide on, then drops back so it resists pulling off. Ridges start past the collar or socket.

The flange is the disk on the tip of the plug, the end inside the tube. Thickness runs back from the tip. Depth is how far it stands out past the plug body. Slots still begin where the tube starts, at the collar or hub.

Each station has a hex pocket for a standard nut. Drop the nut in, then run the screw in from the plug tip. The head seats in the cone and spreads the fingers. The lip keeps the nut from pulling through. Shaft holes include 0.15 mm of clearance on each side. Print one station and test the grip before you make a full roller.

04 / Download

Two STLs. Then the tubing.

Print the plate twice. Print one plug for every tube end. Downloads stay off until the solid checks pass.

From build plate to roller

Test one station first.

01

Print the plate or hub

The STL stands with the axle vertical. Put the flat face on the bed so the collars, or the nut pockets, point up. Do not mirror the STL. The shaft opening is the profile you selected, not a plain circle.

02

Print the plugs

The plug STL is already on its side, with the screw hole horizontal. Leave it that way in the slicer. Skip this print if you chose one piece — the plugs are already on the plate or hub. The screw head enters the cone at the tip. On an axial plate the nut drops into the hex opening on the outer face. On a hub it drops in from the top face.

03

Cut tubes and try the fit

Use the cut length on the preview. The plug is undersized by the clearance you set, then the screw is meant to spread the fingers. Turn on barbs if you want ridges on that outside surface to bite the tube. Adhesive, filament, and the screw you actually have will change the grip. This page does not certify strength or FTC legality.

Before it goes on the robot

Check the current game manual, then have the intake inspected. Geometry is checked for a single closed plate, a single closed plug, and no overlap in the assembly. It is still a shop prototype: no thread form, no measured clamp load, and no guarantee the wedge will hold your tubing.
